title: Which letter-numbers give the numbers that leave three over in fives?
description: Dots are laid in rows of five with three left over, and six cards with the letter k are tested by putting in small values of k. Two cards give exactly the numbers three, eight, thirteen and eighteen. Keeko's doubt is that a card holding a three and a five must fit.
teaching_notes: One idea: test a letter-number by putting in small values of k and comparing with the list of numbers it must give. Watch for students who pick a card only because it holds a three and a five.

video_script.why: The student can describe the numbers that leave remainder three on division by five and now matches that list to a letter-number.
video_script.substitution: Put k equal to zero, one, two, three and four into each card and compare the outputs with the list three, eight, thirteen, eighteen.
video_script.anchor: dots laid in rows of five with three dots left over, the picture of the What Remains part of the book
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko picks the card that holds a three and a five without putting in a value of k; k equal to two gives eleven, which leaves one over.
video_script.payoff_line: Five k plus three and five k minus two both work

final_answer.spoken: five k plus three and five k minus two

maths_rules: remainder 3 on division by 5: 3, 8, 13, 18, 23, each 5 more than the one before
video_script.design: One picture all video: rows of five dots with three over. Six cards on the board; the two that fit light up only in the answer beat.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is from your book, in the part called What Remains.
<bookmark mark='rows'/>Dots are laid in rows of five, and three dots are left over.
<bookmark mark='cards'/>Six cards show letter-numbers, and each one has the letter k.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which cards give exactly the numbers that leave remainder three on division by five?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

narration: <bookmark mark='rows'/>Think of dots laid in rows of five.
The letter k tells us how many full rows we take.
<bookmark mark='put'/>To test a card, we put in small whole numbers for k, starting from zero.
<bookmark mark='test'/>Then we see which numbers come out.

beats.on_screen: Given: numbers that leave remainder 3 on division by 5; cards 3k + 5, 3k - 5, 3k, 5k + 3, 5k - 2, 5k - 3

marks.given: the first three cards are written in a row
marks.last: the last three cards are written beside them

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, six cards. The first three are three k plus five, three k minus five and three k.
<bookmark mark='last'/>The last three are five k plus three, five k minus two and five k minus three.

beats.on_screen: To find: the cards that give exactly the numbers with remainder 3 on division by 5

marks.find: the words To find are written under the cards

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find which cards give exactly the numbers that leave remainder three on division by five.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: the numbers are 3, 8, 13, 18, 23 (each is 5 more than the one before)

marks.list: the numbers 3, 8, 13, 18, 23 are written in a row
marks.five: a plus 5 arrow joins each number to the next

narration: <bookmark mark='list'/>Step one, list the numbers that leave remainder three on division by five.
<bookmark mark='five'/>They are three, eight, thirteen, eighteen and twenty three, each five more than the one before.

marks.try: the card with k equal to 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 is written
marks.out: each output is written under its k and matched to the list

narration: <bookmark mark='try'/>Step two, test the card with five k plus three, putting in k from zero.
<bookmark mark='out'/>Five times zero plus three gives three. Five times one plus three gives eight, and then come thirteen, eighteen and twenty three, the same list.

marks.try: the card with k equal to 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 is written
marks.out: each output is written under its k and matched to the list

narration: <bookmark mark='try'/>Step three, test the card with five k minus two, putting in k from one.
<bookmark mark='out'/>Five times one minus two gives three. Five times two minus two gives eight, and then come thirteen, eighteen and twenty three again.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: k = 2 in the other cards: 3 x 2 + 5 = 11 (remainder 1), 3 x 2 - 5 = 1 (remainder 1), 3 x 2 = 6 (remainder 1), 5 x 2 - 3 = 7 (remainder 2); none leaves 3

marks.plus: three times two plus five gives eleven, with the remainder one marked
marks.minus: three times two minus five gives one, with the remainder one marked
marks.plain: three times two gives six, with the remainder one marked
marks.last: five times two minus three gives seven, with the remainder two marked

narration: <bookmark mark='plus'/>Step four, test the other four cards with k equal to two.
Three times two plus five is eleven, which leaves one. <bookmark mark='minus'/>Three times two minus five is one, which leaves one.
<bookmark mark='plain'/>Three times two is six, which leaves one. <bookmark mark='last'/>Five times two minus three is seven, which leaves two.
None of them leaves remainder three.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 5k + 3 and 5k - 2 (k from 0 and k from 1); the other four do not work

marks.ans: the two cards that fit are boxed
marks.other: the other four cards are crossed out

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Five k plus three and five k minus two both work.
<bookmark mark='other'/>The other four cards do not give exactly those numbers.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the cards
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble points at 3k + 5; k = 2 gives 3 x 2 + 5 = 11; the bubble is crossed out; the dots show 11 as two full rows and one over

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble points at the card 3k + 5
marks.two: k equal to 2 goes into the card and 11 comes out
marks.dots: eleven dots fall into two rows of five with one over
marks.fix: the five on the right of k is lit, then the three that is left over

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks three k plus five fits, because it has a three and a five.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Let us put in k equal to two. Three times two plus five is eleven.
<bookmark mark='dots'/>Eleven dots make two rows of five with one over, not three.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The five must go with k to make the rows, and the three is what is left over.
